Track 1 — SOFTWARE: Build & Innovate

Participants will select a software-oriented problem statement from the set of problem statements provided by the organizers and develop an original, innovative, and functional software-based solution. Solutions may include web applications, mobile applications, AI-powered platforms, intelligent systems, automation tools, data-driven applications, or other innovative software products.

The focus will be on problem understanding, originality, software innovation, functional implementation, user experience, scalability, and practical applicability. Teams should demonstrate a working software prototype and explain its functionality, technical architecture, and potential real-world application.

Software solutions may integrate AI/ML, Generative AI, cloud services, APIs, databases, cybersecurity, automation, or other emerging technologies where they meaningfully enhance the proposed solution.



Featured Problem Statements


PS 1 : Reimagine Government Digital Services for the Next Billion Citizens using Intelligent AI Powered Solutions 

Participants will select an existing government website, portal, application, or citizen-facing digital service and substantially improve its user experience. The focus is on identifying genuine usability, accessibility, navigation, information architecture, mobile experience, and digital-literacy challenges, then transforming the citizen journey into a simpler, clearer, more inclusive, and functional experience. Teams should demonstrate the existing problem, user research, redesigned information architecture and interface, accessibility considerations, and a working implementation or MVP.

PS 2: Reimagine Government Digital Services for the Next Billion Citizens using UI/UX Refinement 

Build for Bharat will feature three specialized competition tracks. Each track approaches the overarching objective of reimagining government digital services and public technology for citizens from a different perspective. Teams may use any suitable technology, while their primary problem-solving objective should align with the selected track.

 

PS 3: Reimagine Government Digital Services for the Next Billion Citizens OPEN INNOVATION

Participants will identify a real citizen or government-service problem where Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning can create meaningful value. Solutions may use intelligent search, RAG-based assistants, recommendation systems, document intelligence, voice AI, multilingual AI, prediction, classification, anomaly detection, or automation. AI must address a clearly defined problem rather than being added as a decorative chatbot. Teams should clearly establish the chain: Problem → Data → AI/ML Approach → Output → Citizen Benefit, while considering reliability, privacy, transparency, and responsible AI.

 

Track 2 — HARDWARE: Build & Innovate

Participants are invited to identify and solve real-world challenges through original, innovative, and functional hardware-based solutions. Teams may select any of the problem statements below and develop a physical prototype that addresses a meaningful need in society, industry, infrastructure, or the environment.

Solutions may incorporate embedded systems, IoT, sensors, robotics, automation, AI/ML, edge computing, communication technologies, or other relevant approaches. Participants are encouraged to explore unconventional ideas, combine multiple technologies, and develop solutions that are affordable, reliable, scalable, and practically applicable.

PS 1: Smart Environmental Monitoring and Protection

Design and develop an innovative hardware-based solution to monitor, analyse, or mitigate environmental challenges. The solution may address air or water quality, pollution, waste management, noise pollution, resource conservation, ecosystem monitoring, or other environmental concerns.

The system should demonstrate how hardware, sensing technologies, intelligent analysis, or automated mechanisms can help detect environmental problems, provide actionable insights, or enable timely intervention.



PS 2: Intelligent Industrial Systems and Automation

Develop a hardware-based solution that improves the efficiency, reliability, safety, or intelligence of industrial and infrastructure systems. Potential applications include equipment monitoring, predictive maintenance, process automation, energy management, fault detection, industrial data acquisition, and intelligent control.

The solution should demonstrate a practical engineering approach to solving an operational challenge, with an emphasis on reliability, affordability, adaptability, and real-world deployment.

PS 3: Smart Safety, Hazard Detection and Risk Prevention

Build an innovative hardware-based system that identifies potential hazards, monitors dangerous conditions, or helps prevent accidents in workplaces, public spaces, transportation systems, or other high-risk environments.

Applications may include mine safety, fire and gas hazard detection, electrical safety, structural risk monitoring, industrial worker protection, confined-space safety, and early warning systems. Solutions may use sensors, embedded intelligence, robotics, communication networks, or automated response mechanisms.

PS 4: Intelligent Healthcare, Assistive Technology and Human Safety

Design and prototype a hardware-based solution that improves human safety, health monitoring, accessibility, independent living, or emergency assistance.

Possible applications include assistive devices for people with disabilities, elderly care systems, wearable safety devices, remote physiological monitoring, emergency alert systems, rehabilitation aids, and intelligent personal assistance. Solutions should prioritise usability, affordability, reliability, and the needs of their intended users.

PS 5: Smart Infrastructure, Disaster Management and Resilient Communities

Develop a hardware-based solution that addresses challenges in public infrastructure, urban development, transportation, agriculture, water management, disaster preparedness, or emergency response.

Potential applications include flood and landslide monitoring, rockfall prediction, infrastructure inspection, intelligent traffic systems, precision agriculture, water leakage detection, search-and-rescue robotics, and resource optimisation. The solution should demonstrate how physical systems and intelligent technologies can improve situational awareness, reduce risks, or support faster and better-informed decsisions.

Expectations for All Problem Statements

  • Problem understanding: Clearly identify the real-world challenge, its intended users, and the limitations of existing approaches.
  • Originality and innovation: Develop a meaningful solution rather than merely reproducing an existing product or demonstration.
  • Functional hardware prototype: Demonstrate working physical components and the core functionality of the proposed solution.
  • Concept-Based Prototyping: Teams with limited access to hardware may demonstrate their solution through a concept model, simulation, proof of concept, or a prototype using minimal available hardware. In such cases, evaluation will place greater emphasis on the originality, feasibility, technical approach, problem-solving potential, and real-world applicability of the idea.
  • Engineering implementation: Explain the hardware architecture, operating principle, component selection, and integration of software or intelligent technologies.
  • Reliability and practical applicability: Demonstrate the solution under realistic test conditions and identify its limitations.
  • Scalability and impact: Explain how the prototype could evolve into an affordable, deployable solution with measurable real-world benefits.

Teams are not restricted to the example applications listed under each problem statement. They may propose any relevant application that fits the chosen problem domain and demonstrates a substantial hardware component.

The primary evaluation focus is the quality of the problem-solving approach, hardware innovation, functional implementation, and practical impact, not the complexity of the technology used.

 

Track Flexibility

Teams are not required to use every technology or component. A software solution may incorporate hardware where relevant, and a hardware solution may use software or AI as supporting components. The primary track should be determined by the core nature of the proposed solution.

 

Format & Process

  • Round 0 – Registration & Idea Screening (Online): Teams submit their initial idea. Shortlisting is based on problem relevance, innovation, feasibility and impact.
  • Round 1 – Discover, Define, Design & Build (Offline): Shortlisted teams build a working prototype. Mid-event evaluation and shortlisting follow.
  • Final Round – Demo & Jury Q&A: Each team gets a 10-minute presentation with live demo, then a 4-minute jury Q&A.

Eligibility & Rules

  • Teams of upto 4 members.
  • Solutions must be original and built during the hackathon.
  • A working prototype is mandatory for the final evaluation. Concept-only submissions will not qualify.
  • AI/ML must solve a clearly identified problem, not serve as a decorative add-on.
  • Participants must follow event discipline and the organizers' decisions are final.

Prizes & Perks

  • Prize pool of ₹1,20,000 across both tracks (Top 3 winners per track)
  • Certificates for participants, finalists and winners
  • Goodies, mentorship from industry professionals, and industry speaker sessions
  • Meals and refreshments throughout the event
